title: ContextWell system
summary: Translating the Spectrum of Contextual Well-being framework into an applied AI system for high-pressure environments such as medical education.
problem: High-pressure environments — like medical education — often ask people to make good decisions without giving them the contextual support to do so.
idea: Model well-being as a functional capacity, using the Spectrum of Contextual Well-being (SCW) to map how perception and judgment shift across different environments.
building: An applied AI system that turns the SCW framework into adaptive feedback for people working under pressure, starting with medical education.
stage: In active development as part of ContextWell Lab.

title: AI Contextual Framework
summary: A zoning approach to AI governance, reframing oversight as a dimension of well-being efficacy — presented at AAAI/ACM AIES 2025.
problem: AI governance is often framed purely as compliance — a checklist rather than a design principle that actually protects the people affected.
idea: A zoning approach that reframes human oversight as a dimension of well-being efficacy, not just a regulatory requirement.
building: A conceptual framework, presented at AAAI/ACM AIES 2025, intended to inform how agency-preserving AI systems get designed and evaluated.
stage: Published and presented; being extended into applied design guidance.
